The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[Nihon Shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort = [[Ugayafukiaezu]] }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>

T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />

However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

{{Short description|Japanese kami}} {{Distinguish|Tamakushi-hime}} {{more citations needed|date=July 2020}} {{Expand language|langcode=ja|otherarticle=|section=|date=October 2020|fa=|topic=|nodoc=|no interwiki=}}
{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort = [[Ugayafukiaezu]] }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>

{{Short description|Japanese kami}} {{Distinguish|Tamakushi-hime}} {{more citations needed|date=July 2020}} {{Expand language|langcode=ja|otherarticle=|section=|date=October 2020|fa=|topic=|nodoc=|no interwiki=}}
{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort = [[Ugayafukiaezu]] }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort = [[Ugayafukiaezu]] }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>

However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

{{Short description|Japanese kami}} {{Distinguish|Tamakushi-hime}} {{more citations needed|date=July 2020}} {{Expand language|langcode=ja|otherarticle=|section=|date=October 2020|fa=|topic=|nodoc=|no interwiki=}}
{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort = [[Ugayafukiaezu]] }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>

Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.

{{Short description|Japanese kami}} {{Distinguish|Tamakushi-hime}} {{more citations needed|date=July 2020}} {{Expand language|langcode=ja|otherarticle=|section=|date=October 2020|fa=|topic=|nodoc=|no interwiki=}}
{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort = [[Ugayafukiaezu]] }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[:en:Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>

Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
