{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q3082751]] Wikidata name: Tamayori-bime [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:49, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese kami}} {{Distinguish|Tamakushi-hime}} {{more citations needed|date=July 2020}} {{Expand language|langcode=ja|otherarticle=|section=|date=October 2020|fa=|topic=|nodoc=|no interwiki=}}
{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort =[[Ugayafukiaezu]]; {{ill|Hoori|qid=Q1051960}}; {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|qid=Q1373935}}| image = File:Tamayori hime statue detail.JPG | gender = {{ill|female|qid=Q6581072}} | parents = {{ill|Watatsumi|qid=Q1474187}} | offspring = {{ill|Hiko Itsuse no Mikoto|qid=Q10881970}}; {{ill|Inai no Mikoto|qid=Q11420805}}; {{ill|Jimmu|qid=Q200188}}; {{ill|Mikeiri no Mikoto|qid=Q11071195}} }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[:en:Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort =[[Ugayafukiaezu]]; {{ill|Hoori|qid=Q1051960}}; {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|qid=Q1373935}}| image = File:Tamayori hime statue detail.JPG | gender = {{ill|female|qid=Q6581072}} | parents = {{ill|Watatsumi|qid=Q1474187}} | offspring = {{ill|Hiko Itsuse no Mikoto|qid=Q10881970}}; {{ill|Inai no Mikoto|qid=Q11420805}}; {{ill|Jimmu|qid=Q200188}}; {{ill|Mikeiri no Mikoto|qid=Q11071195}} | equivalent5 = {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|qid=Q106241380}} }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[:en:Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q3082751]] Wikidata name: Tamayori-bime [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:49, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese kami}} {{Distinguish|Tamakushi-hime}} {{more citations needed|date=July 2020}} {{Expand language|langcode=ja|otherarticle=|section=|date=October 2020|fa=|topic=|nodoc=|no interwiki=}}
{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort =[[Ugayafukiaezu]]; {{ill|Hoori|qid=Q1051960}}; {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|qid=Q1373935}}| image = File:Tamayori hime statue detail.JPG | gender = {{ill|female|qid=Q6581072}} | parents = {{ill|Watatsumi|qid=Q1474187}} | offspring = {{ill|Hiko Itsuse no Mikoto|qid=Q10881970}}; {{ill|Inai no Mikoto|qid=Q11420805}}; {{ill|Jimmu|qid=Q200188}}; {{ill|Mikeiri no Mikoto|qid=Q11071195}} | equivalent5_type = Japanese | equivalent5 = {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|qid=Q106241380}} }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[:en:Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>

This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q3082751]] Wikidata name: Tamayori-bime [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:49, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese kami}} {{Distinguish|Tamakushi-hime}} {{more citations needed|date=July 2020}} {{Expand language|langcode=ja|otherarticle=|section=|date=October 2020|fa=|topic=|nodoc=|no interwiki=}}
{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort =[[Ugayafukiaezu]]; {{ill|Hoori|qid=Q1051960}}; {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|qid=Q1373935}}| image = File:Tamayori hime statue detail.JPG | gender = {{ill|female|qid=Q6581072}} | parents = {{ill|Watatsumi|qid=Q1474187}} | offspring = {{ill|Hiko Itsuse no Mikoto|qid=Q10881970}}; {{ill|Inai no Mikoto|qid=Q11420805}}; {{ill|Jimmu|qid=Q200188}}; {{ill|Mikeiri no Mikoto|qid=Q11071195}} | equivalent5_type = Japanese | equivalent5 = {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|qid=Q106241380}} }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=|1=Ryūkō Myōjinsha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11679214}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[:en:Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=|1=Utsushi Hikanasaku no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86736058}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>

{{Otheruses|神武天皇の母のタマヨリビメ|その他のタマヨリビメと呼ばれる人物・女神|タマヨリビメ}}{{基礎情報 日本の神 | 名 = 玉依毘売 ／ 玉依姫 | 世代名 = | 先代 = | 次代 = | 神祇 = [[国津神]] | 全名 = 玉依毘売 ／ 玉依姫 | 別名 = 玉依毘売命 | 別称 = | 神階 = | 神格 = [[巫女]]、[[蛇神]]（[[龍神]]） | 陵所 = [[日南市]]に伝承あり | 父 = [[大綿津見神]]（綿津見大神、海童、豊玉彦） | 親 = | 配偶者 = [[鵜草葺不合命]]、[[火折尊]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 子 = [[五瀬命]]
[[稲氷命]]
[[御毛沼命]]
[[若御毛沼命]]（[[神武天皇]]）
[[武位起命]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 宮 = 綿津見神の宮、[[宮浦神社 (日南市)|宮浦神社]] | 神社 = [[霧島神宮]]、[[高千穂神社]]等 | 御利益 = | 記紀 = | 関連氏族 = [[皇室]]、[[阿曇氏]] |画像=Tamyorihime shinbutsu-zue.jpg|画像説明=（『神仏図会』）}} '''タマヨリビメ'''（'''玉依毘売'''、『[[古事記]]』）または'''タマヨリヒメ'''（'''玉依姫'''、『[[日本書紀]]』）は、[[日本神話]]に登場する[[神 (神道)|女神]]。[[神武天皇]]（初代[[天皇]]）の母として知られる。 == 概要 == 『[[古事記]]』では'''玉依毘売'''、'''玉依毘売命'''、『[[日本書紀]]』では'''玉依姫'''と表記される。 [[神武天皇]]（初代[[天皇]]）の母であり、天皇の祖母である[[トヨタマヒメ|豊玉毘売]]の妹。 名義は「神霊が依り憑く巫女」と考えられる。[[大物主|大物主神]]の妻である[[玉櫛媛|活玉依毘売]]や、『[[山城国風土記]]』逸文に見える[[タマヨリビメ|玉依日売]]と同じく、この名前を持つ者は神と通婚する巫女的神性を持つとされる。なお皇統が穀霊で続き、玉依毘売の御子も「五瀬命」（厳稲の命）、「稲氷命」（稲霊の命）、「御毛沼命」（御食主の命）、「若御毛沼命」（若御食主の命）であることから、特に穀霊を依り憑かせる巫女であったと考えられる{{Cite book |和書 |author=西宮一民|authorlink=西宮一民 |title=新潮日本古典集成 第27回 古事記 |date=1979-6-12 |publisher=[[新潮社]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages={{要ページ番号|date=2019年3月}}}}。 '''[[宮浦神社 (日南市)|宮浦神社]]'''（[[宮崎県]][[日南市]]）は玉依姫の住居跡といわれる[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ 伝承地詳細70　タマヨリヒメ陵　日南市] - 100の伝承地 - ひむか神話街道（2018年7月24日午後6時41分（[[日本標準時|JST]]）閲覧）。また[[宮崎県]][[日南市]]に玉依姫の[[陵墓]]であると伝えられる場所がある。 [[龍口明神社]]では[[龍神]]を束ねる[[海人族|海神族]]の祖先とされ、また姫自身も龍神として崇められている[http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/御祭神]（2019年8月6日22時19分閲覧）。 == 系譜 == 『[[記紀]]』によれば、父は[[綿津見神]]で母に関する記載はないが、姉に[[豊玉毘売命]]がいる。 * 夫：'''[[彦波瀲武鸕鶿草葺不合尊]]'''（ひこなぎさたけうがやふきあわせず の みこと/-ふきあえず の みこと、『古事記』では日子波限建鵜葺草葺不合命） - 『日本書紀』 *: 火折尊の子。 ** 子：[[彦五瀬命]]（ひこいつせ の みこと、『古事記』では五瀬命） - 『日本書紀』 **: [[神武東征]]の際に賊の矢にあたって薨じた。 ** 子：[[稲飯命]]（いない の みこと、『古事記』では稲氷命） - 『日本書紀』 **: 韓地に渡ったが、神武東征の際に鋤持神となったとも。 ** 子：[[三毛入野命]]（みけいりぬ の みこと、三毛野命、『古事記』では御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』、『先代旧事本紀』 **: 神武東征の際に[[常世郷]]へ行った。 ** 子：'''[[神日本磐余彦尊]]'''（かむやまといわれびこ の みこと、『古事記』では和風諱号を神倭伊波礼毘古、名を若御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』 **: のちの'''神武天皇（初代[[天皇]]）''' === 系図 ===

（神武天皇）}} {{familytree|border=0| | | | | | | | | | | | | |!| | | | | | | }} {{familytree|border=0| | | | | | | | | | | | | 001 | | | | | |001=（子孫は[[皇室]]）}} {{familytree/end}}
* {{Bgcolor|#F2CEE0|赤背景}}は女性。
出典：{{Sfn|古代豪族系図集覧|p=7}} == 記録 == === 古事記 === 『[[古事記]]』によれば、[[豊玉毘売命]]は出産後、大きなサメの本体をあらわにしてしまったのを恥じ、子（[[鵜葺草葺不合命]]）を置いて去ったが、のちに妹の'''玉依毘売命'''を遣わして歌を献り、子を養わせた。のちに鵜葺草葺不合命は玉依毘売命をめとり、四子を生んだという。 === 日本書紀 === 『[[日本書紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫は[[火折尊]]との間の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産むために海から海辺に来たが、この時豊玉姫は妹の'''玉依姫'''を従えていた。のちに玉依姫は鸕鶿草葺不合尊（玉依姫から見れば[[甥]]にあたる）の妃となり四子を生んだという。 また、第10段の第1の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子（鸕鶿草葺不合尊）を置いて海にかえったが、その際に玉依姫を留めて鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第3の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子を置いて海に去ったが、その後、玉依姫を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第4の一書では、「一云」として、豊玉姫は出産後、子を自ら抱いて海に去ったが、のちに玉依姫に子を抱かせて陸に送り出したとする。 === 先代旧事本紀 === 『[[先代旧事本紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫命は火折尊の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産んだ後、子を置いて自ら抱いて海に去った（または'''玉依姫命'''を留めて子を養わせて去り、のちに玉依姫命に子を持たせて陸に送り出した）。のちに豊玉姫命は玉依姫命を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせた。この時、玉依姫命と火折尊との間に武位起命がうまれた。のちに玉依姫命は自らが養った鸕鶿草葺不合尊の妃となり、四子を生んだという。 [[武位起命]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 宮 = 綿津見神の宮、[[宮浦神社 (日南市)|宮浦神社]] | 神社 = [[霧島神宮]]、[[高千穂神社]]等 | 御利益 = | 記紀 = | 関連氏族 = [[皇室]]、[[阿曇氏]] |画像=Tamyorihime shinbutsu-zue.jpg|画像説明=（『神仏図会』）}} '''タマヨリビメ'''は、「神霊が依り憑く女性（[[巫女]]）」を意味する普通名詞であり、古代の神話・伝承で神との間に子をもうけた様々な女性がそう呼ばれるが{{Kotobank|1=玉依姫}}、本項では、[[日本神話]]に登場する[[神武天皇]]の母として知られる'''タマヨリビメ'''（'''玉依毘売'''、『[[古事記]]』）または'''タマヨリヒメ'''（'''玉依姫'''、『[[日本書紀]]』）について述べる。 == 概要 == タマヨリビメの名は外にも記紀神話や[[風土記]]で別存在の名として見られ、[[倉塚曄子]]によると、タマヨリビメとは「神霊が依り憑く女性」を意味し、「祭儀の際、神降臨の秘儀に立ち会う巫女が、神話的には神に感精してその子を生む母として形象化されたもの」であり、物語の中では固有名詞、名前のように扱われているが、普通名詞と考えた方が正しい。本項のタマヨリビメは、『[[古事記]]』では'''玉依毘売'''、'''玉依毘売命'''、『[[日本書紀]]』では'''玉依姫'''と表記される。海の神の娘であり、若御毛沼命（[[神武天皇]]）の母、天孫[[彦火火出見尊]]との間に[[彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊]]を生んだ[[トヨタマヒメ|豊玉毘売]]の妹。 皇統が穀霊で続き、玉依毘売の御子も「五瀬命」（厳稲の命）、「稲氷命」（稲霊の命）、「御毛沼命」（御食主の命）、「若御毛沼命」（若御食主の命）であることから、本項のタマヨリビメは、特に穀霊を依り憑かせる巫女であったと考えられる{{Cite book |和書 |author=西宮一民|authorlink=西宮一民 |title=新潮日本古典集成 第27回 古事記 |date=1979-6-12 |publisher=[[新潮社]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages={{要ページ番号|date=2019年3月}}}}。 '''[[宮浦神社 (日南市)|宮浦神社]]'''（[[宮崎県]][[日南市]]）はタマヨリビメの住居跡といわれる[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ 伝承地詳細70　タマヨリヒメ陵　日南市] - 100の伝承地 - ひむか神話街道（2018年7月24日午後6時41分（[[日本標準時|JST]]）閲覧）。また[[宮崎県]][[日南市]]にタマヨリビメの[[陵墓]]であると伝えられる場所がある。 [[龍口明神社]]では[[龍神]]を束ねる[[海人族|海神族]]の祖先とされ、また姫自身も龍神として崇められている[http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/御祭神]（2019年8月6日22時19分閲覧）。 == 系譜 == 『[[記紀]]』によれば、父は[[綿津見神]]で母に関する記載はないが、姉に[[豊玉毘売命]]がいる。 * 夫：'''[[彦波瀲武鸕鶿草葺不合尊]]'''（ひこなぎさたけうがやふきあわせず の みこと/-ふきあえず の みこと、『古事記』では日子波限建鵜葺草葺不合命） - 『日本書紀』 *: 火折尊の子。 ** 子：[[彦五瀬命]]（ひこいつせ の みこと、『古事記』では五瀬命） - 『日本書紀』 **: [[神武東征]]の際に賊の矢にあたって薨じた。 ** 子：[[稲飯命]]（いない の みこと、『古事記』では稲氷命） - 『日本書紀』 **: 韓地に渡ったが、神武東征の際に鋤持神となったとも。 ** 子：[[三毛入野命]]（みけいりぬ の みこと、三毛野命、『古事記』では御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』、『先代旧事本紀』 **: 神武東征の際に[[常世郷]]へ行った。 ** 子：'''[[神日本磐余彦尊]]'''（かむやまといわれびこ の みこと、『古事記』では和風諱号を神倭伊波礼毘古、名を若御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』 **: のちの'''神武天皇（初代[[天皇]]）''' === 系図 ===

* {{Bgcolor|#F2CEE0|赤背景}}は女性。
出典：{{Sfn|古代豪族系図集覧|p=7}} == 記録 == === 古事記 === 『[[古事記]]』によれば、[[豊玉毘売命]]は出産後、大きなサメの本体をあらわにしてしまったのを恥じ、子（[[鵜葺草葺不合命]]）を置いて去ったが、のちに妹の'''玉依毘売命'''を遣わして歌を献り、子を養わせた。のちに鵜葺草葺不合命は玉依毘売命をめとり、四子を生んだという。 === 日本書紀 === 『[[日本書紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫は[[火折尊]]との間の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産むために海から海辺に来たが、この時豊玉姫は妹の'''玉依姫'''を従えていた。のちに玉依姫は鸕鶿草葺不合尊（玉依姫から見れば[[甥]]にあたる）の妃となり四子を生んだという。 また、第10段の第1の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子（鸕鶿草葺不合尊）を置いて海にかえったが、その際に玉依姫を留めて鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第3の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子を置いて海に去ったが、その後、玉依姫を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第4の一書では、「一云」として、豊玉姫は出産後、子を自ら抱いて海に去ったが、のちに玉依姫に子を抱かせて陸に送り出したとする。 === 先代旧事本紀 === 『[[先代旧事本紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫命は火折尊の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産んだ後、子を置いて自ら抱いて海に去った（または'''玉依姫命'''を留めて子を養わせて去り、のちに玉依姫命に子を持たせて陸に送り出した）。のちに豊玉姫命は玉依姫命を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせた。この時、玉依姫命と火折尊との間に武位起命がうまれた。のちに玉依姫命は自らが養った鸕鶿草葺不合尊の妃となり、四子を生んだという。 [[武位起命]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 宮 = 綿津見神の宮、[[宮浦神社 (日南市)|宮浦神社]] | 神社 = [[霧島神宮]]、[[高千穂神社]]等 | 御利益 = | 記紀 = | 関連氏族 = [[皇室]]、[[阿曇氏]] |画像=Tamyorihime shinbutsu-zue.jpg|画像説明=（『神仏図会』）}} '''タマヨリビメ'''は、「神霊が依り憑く女性（[[巫女]]）」を意味する普通名詞であり、古代の神話・伝承で神との間に子をもうけた様々な女性がそう呼ばれるが{{Kotobank|1=玉依姫}}、本項では、[[日本神話]]に登場する[[神武天皇]]の母として知られる'''タマヨリビメ'''（'''玉依毘売'''、『[[古事記]]』）または'''タマヨリヒメ'''（'''玉依姫'''、『[[日本書紀]]』）について述べる。 == 概要 == タマヨリビメの名は外にも記紀神話や[[風土記]]で別存在の名として見られ、[[倉塚曄子]]によると、タマヨリビメとは「神霊が依り憑く女性」を意味し、「祭儀の際、神降臨の秘儀に立ち会う巫女が、神話的には神に感精してその子を生む母として形象化されたもの」であり、物語の中では固有名詞、名前のように扱われているが、普通名詞と考えた方が正しい。本項のタマヨリビメは、『[[古事記]]』では'''玉依毘売'''、'''玉依毘売命'''、『[[日本書紀]]』では'''玉依姫'''と表記される。海の神の娘であり、天孫[[彦火火出見尊]]との間に[[彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊]]を生んだ[[トヨタマヒメ|豊玉毘売]]の妹で、養育した甥の彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊と結婚し若御毛沼命（[[神武天皇]]）をもうけた。 皇統が穀霊で続き、玉依毘売の御子も「五瀬命」（厳稲の命）、「稲氷命」（稲霊の命）、「御毛沼命」（御食主の命）、「若御毛沼命」（若御食主の命）であることから、本項のタマヨリビメは、特に穀霊を依り憑かせる巫女であったと考えられる{{Cite book |和書 |author=西宮一民|authorlink=西宮一民 |title=新潮日本古典集成 第27回 古事記 |date=1979-6-12 |publisher=[[新潮社]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages={{要ページ番号|date=2019年3月}}}}。 '''[[宮浦神社 (日南市)|宮浦神社]]'''（[[宮崎県]][[日南市]]）はタマヨリビメの住居跡といわれる[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ 伝承地詳細70　タマヨリヒメ陵　日南市] - 100の伝承地 - ひむか神話街道（2018年7月24日午後6時41分（[[日本標準時|JST]]）閲覧）。また[[宮崎県]][[日南市]]にタマヨリビメの[[陵墓]]であると伝えられる場所がある。 [[龍口明神社]]では[[龍神]]を束ねる[[海人族|海神族]]の祖先とされ、また姫自身も龍神として崇められている[http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/御祭神]（2019年8月6日22時19分閲覧）。 == 系譜 == 『[[記紀]]』によれば、父は[[綿津見神]]で母に関する記載はないが、姉に[[豊玉毘売命]]がいる。 * 夫：'''[[彦波瀲武鸕鶿草葺不合尊]]'''（ひこなぎさたけうがやふきあわせず の みこと/-ふきあえず の みこと、『古事記』では日子波限建鵜葺草葺不合命） - 『日本書紀』 *: 火折尊の子。 ** 子：[[彦五瀬命]]（ひこいつせ の みこと、『古事記』では五瀬命） - 『日本書紀』 **: [[神武東征]]の際に賊の矢にあたって薨じた。 ** 子：[[稲飯命]]（いない の みこと、『古事記』では稲氷命） - 『日本書紀』 **: 韓地に渡ったが、神武東征の際に鋤持神となったとも。 ** 子：[[三毛入野命]]（みけいりぬ の みこと、三毛野命、『古事記』では御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』、『先代旧事本紀』 **: 神武東征の際に[[常世郷]]へ行った。 ** 子：'''[[神日本磐余彦尊]]'''（かむやまといわれびこ の みこと、『古事記』では和風諱号を神倭伊波礼毘古、名を若御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』 **: のちの'''神武天皇（初代[[天皇]]）''' === 系図 ===

* {{Bgcolor|#F2CEE0|赤背景}}は女性。
出典：{{Sfn|古代豪族系図集覧|p=7}} == 記録 == === 古事記 === 『[[古事記]]』によれば、[[豊玉毘売命]]は出産後、大きなサメの本体をあらわにしてしまったのを恥じ、子（[[鵜葺草葺不合命]]）を置いて去ったが、のちに妹の'''玉依毘売命'''を遣わして歌を献り、子を養わせた。のちに鵜葺草葺不合命は玉依毘売命をめとり、四子を生んだという。 === 日本書紀 === 『[[日本書紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫は[[火折尊]]との間の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産むために海から海辺に来たが、この時豊玉姫は妹の'''玉依姫'''を従えていた。のちに玉依姫は鸕鶿草葺不合尊（玉依姫から見れば[[甥]]にあたる）の妃となり四子を生んだという。 また、第10段の第1の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子（鸕鶿草葺不合尊）を置いて海にかえったが、その際に玉依姫を留めて鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第3の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子を置いて海に去ったが、その後、玉依姫を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第4の一書では、「一云」として、豊玉姫は出産後、子を自ら抱いて海に去ったが、のちに玉依姫に子を抱かせて陸に送り出したとする。 === 先代旧事本紀 === 『[[先代旧事本紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫命は火折尊の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産んだ後、子を置いて自ら抱いて海に去った（または'''玉依姫命'''を留めて子を養わせて去り、のちに玉依姫命に子を持たせて陸に送り出した）。のちに豊玉姫命は玉依姫命を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせた。この時、玉依姫命と火折尊との間に武位起命がうまれた。のちに玉依姫命は自らが養った鸕鶿草葺不合尊の妃となり、四子を生んだという。 {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q3082751]] Wikidata name: Tamayori-bime [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:49, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese kami}} {{Distinguish|Tamakushi-hime}} {{more citations needed|date=July 2020}} {{Expand language|langcode=ja|otherarticle=|section=|date=October 2020|fa=|topic=|nodoc=|no interwiki=}}
{{Infobox deity | type = Shinto | father = [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] | children = [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], [[Itsuse no Mikoto]], [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]], [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] | consort =[[Ugayafukiaezu]]; {{ill|Hoori|qid=Q1051960}}; {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|qid=Q1373935}}| image = File:Tamayori hime statue detail.JPG | gender = {{ill|female|qid=Q6581072}} | parents = {{ill|Watatsumi|qid=Q1474187}} | offspring = {{ill|Hiko Itsuse no Mikoto|qid=Q10881970}}; {{ill|Inai no Mikoto|qid=Q11420805}}; {{ill|Jimmu|qid=Q200188}}; {{ill|Mikeiri no Mikoto|qid=Q11071195}} | equivalent5_type = Japanese | equivalent5 = {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|qid=Q106241380}} }}'''Tamayori-hime''' is a [[:en:Goddess|Goddess]] in [[Japanese mythology]]. Her name is spelled as {{Nihongo2|玉依毘売命}} in the [[Kojiki]] and {{Nihongo2|玉依姫}} in the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]].
Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] and the younger sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]]. When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband [[Hoori]], she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son [[Ugayafukiaezu]], although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Akima |first1=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |journal=Japan Review |volume=4 |issue=4 |page=143 |issn=0915-0986 |jstor=25790929}}</ref> When the child grew up, he married his aunt, who bore him four children, the youngest of which became [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]], the first emperor of Japan.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Allan |first1=Tony |last2=Phillips |first2=Charles |last3=Kerrigan |first3=Michael |title=Realm of the Rising Sun: Japanese Myth |date=2000 |publisher=[[Time-Life Books]] |isbn=9780705436632 |pages=68–69}}</ref>
== Summary == She is the mother of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[:en:Emperor|Emperor]]) and the sister of [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]], the Emperor's grandmother. Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.<ref name=":0" />
The word ''tamayori-hime'' is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities. The Japanese folklorist [[Kunio Yanagita]] espoused the view that ''tamayori-hime'' means "a consecrated women to whom a spirit descends" and that the intimate relationships between the two helped generate belief in mother-son pair deities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hosoi |first=Y. T. |date=1976 |title=The Sacred Tree in Japanese Prehistory |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1062238 |journal=History of Religions |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=95–119 |issn=0018-2710}}</ref> In addition, since the line of succession is based on grain spirits, and the sons of Tamayorihime are also named {{Nihongo|2=厳稲の命|3=Gose no mikoto}}, {{Nihongo|Inahiron no mikoto|稲氷の命}}, {{Nihongo|Mogonuma no mikoto|御食主の命}}, and {{Nihongo|Wakamogonuma no mikoto|若御食主の命}}, it is thought that they were priestesses who possessed grain spirits.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Kazutami Nishimiya]] |title=Shincho Japanese Classics, Vol. 27: Kojiki |date=1979-06-12 |publisher=[[Shinchosha]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages=}}{{missing page number|date=March 2019}}</ref>
Miyaura Shrine ([[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]]) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.<ref name="shinwa">[http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/kaido/100map/legendlist/070/ Tradition Site Detail 70: Tamayorihime Mausoleum, Nichinan City] - 100 Tradition Sites - Himuka Mythical Road (viewed at 6:41 pm ([[:en:Japan Standard Time|JST]]) on 24 July 2018)</ref> There is also a place in [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan City]] that is said to be the [[:en:Mausoleum|Mausoleum]] of Princess Tamayori.<ref name="shinwa" />
At the {{ill|Ryūkomyō Shrine|ja|龍口明神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūkomyō Shrine|qq=|1=Ryūkō Myōjinsha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11679214}}, she is considered the ancestor of the [[:en:Sea People (Japan)|Kaijin Tribe]], which unites [[Ryūjin|Ryujin]], and the princess herself is worshipped as Ryujin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gozuryu.com/gosaishin.php/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A5%AD%E7%A5%9E|title=御祭神|龍口明神社|website=gozuryu.com}}</ref>
== Genealogy == According to the Kiki, her father is [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]]. Her mother's name is unknown but her older sister is [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]]. The {{ill|Yamato Shukune|ja|宇都志日金拆命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Shukune|qq=|1=Utsushi Hikanasaku no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86736058}} and [[Uminao]] genealogies in the Hyakuke Genealogy and the Shukune and Uminao genealogies in the Shukune and Uminao have {{ill|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsushihikanasaku|qq=}} (Hotakami-no-mikoto, ancestor of the [[Azumi people]]) and {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari Kuni-no-miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], etc.) as brothers. However, it is believed that [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] and [[Tamakushi-hime|Tamayori-hime]] were sisters who became the wives of [[Hoori|Hienori-no-mikoto]], and based on genealogical comparisons with other clans, there is a theory that they were actually daughters rather than sisters of Utsushihikkinasei-no-mikoto.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Genealogy of the Gods and the Early Branching Process of the Kaijin Clan, Kojiki no Bosama, 2011. |url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/yamasho/ookuni1.htm|title=天照大神と大国主神の関係 {{!}} ─筑紫国と高天原神話・日向三代神話─}}</ref> ([[Tamayori-hime (Hyuga myth)#考考|see below]]).
* Husband: [[Ugayafukiaezu]] (in the Kojiki: 日子波限建鵜葺草合不合命) - "Nihonshoki" *: Son of [[Hoori]]. **Child: [[Itsuse no Mikoto]] (Mikoto Hikotose, Mikoto Gose in "Kojiki")-"Nihon Shoki" *** He was killed by a bandit's arrow during the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]]. ** Son: [[:en:Inahi no Mikoto|Inahi no Mikoto]] (Inai-no-mikoto in [[Kojiki]]) - [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]] ***He went to Korea, but he became a plow god during the Jimmu's Eastern Expedition **Child: [[Mikeiri no Mikoto]] **Child: [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]
=== Different theories ===
* Husband: [[Hoori|Hori-no-mikoto]] - [[Kujiki]] *: Son of [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. ** Child: Inauguration of Takeshi (Mikoto Takeiki, Mikoto Takekura)-"Kujiki Kujiki" **: The ancestor of Oya Kuni-no-miyatsuko . However, in " Kujiki [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen]]", Kunigami is treated as a territory, and in various genealogy, it is a child of Tamayori-hime's brother, Nunodome Tamayori.<ref>宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族 第1節 海神族 6倭国造倭直、大倭忌寸」『古代 氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1286-1288頁</ref> The article in "Kujiki Kunigami" seems to be a misrepresentation。
=== Family tree === {{three generations of Hyuga}}
== Examination == According to the Chronicles, Tamayori Biyori-no-mikoto's husband, Ukusabifune no Mikoto, was the grandson of Emperor Ninigi-no-mikoto, and Emperor Jimmu was his great-grandson. However, if we compare the generations of those who accompanied the {{ill|Kume clan|lt=descendants of the gods|ja|久米氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kume clan|qq=}} with those involved in the [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu East Expedition]], we find that the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi-ren]], [[Inbe clan|Imbibe shu]], [[Nakatomi clan|Kume nao]], and other related clans are always grandfather and grandson, and only the imperial lineage is somehow one generation older. However, intergenerational marriages between nephews and their aunts are rare and cannot be said to be a regular occurrence, and even in the few cases where they have occurred, there has never been a marriage with a mother's younger half-sister. This has led some to believe that the genealogy of Ukusa-thatching-furinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu is a corruption of the tradition of sister marriages common among horsemen, and that Toyotamabihime and Tamayoribihime were sisters who married [[Hoori]], with the former giving birth to [[Ugayafukiaezu]] and the latter to Emperor Jimmu and his siblings. According to this theory, Ukusabufurinushi-no-mikoto and Emperor Jimmu were both sons of Hiotorinushi-no-mikoto, making them half-brothers, and the number of generations is consistent with those of other related authors.<ref>Tsuo Hoga, "Chapter 7: Genealogy of the Jinmu Clan", in The Original Image of the "Jinmu Eastward Conquest", Aogaki Shuppan, 2006, pp. 303-305.</ref>
== Records ==
=== Kojiki === According to ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]] left her child ([[Ugayafukiaezu]]) after giving birth, but later sent her sister, Tamayoribirinomikoto, to offer her a song and provide for her child. Later, Ukagusabuhuri-no-mikoto married Tamayoribihime and had four children with her.
=== Nihon Shoki === According to the [[:en:Nihon shoki|Nihon shoki]], Toyotama-hime came to the seashore from the sea to give birth to her child with [[Hoori]], a thatch-thatched goddess, but at this time Toyotama-hime was accompanied by her sister, Tamayori-hime. Later, Tamayorihime became the consort of [[:en:Nephew|Nephew]] of the goddess of thatched roofs (from Tamayorihime's point of view) and gave birth to four children.
According to the first sentence of the tenth section, after giving birth to her child, Toyotama-hime returned to the sea, leaving her child behind.
According to the third book, Toyotama-hime left her child at sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayor-ihime to give a song to Fire Ori and nourish the king.
In the fourth book of the same name, the story goes that Toyotama-hime took the child in her arms and left for the sea after giving birth, but later sent Tamayori-hime to take the child in her arms and send her back to land.
=== The Old Chronicle of the First Age === According to the [[Kujiki|Old History of Japan]], Toyotamahime-no-mikoto gave birth to a child, a child of Hiori-no-mikoto, and then left the child in her arms and went to the sea (or let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take care of the child and leave, and later let Tamayori-hime-no-mikoto take the child and send it to land). Later, Toyotama-hime no Mikoto sent Tamayorihime no Mikoto to give a song to Hiori no Mikoto, and have her feed the infant Kusabufuri no Mikoto. It was at this time that Tamayorihime no Mikoto and Hiori no Mikoto were born. Later, Tamayorihime-no-mikoto became the wife of the Goddess of Arms, whom she had nurtured, and gave birth to four children.

{{Otheruses|神武天皇の母のタマヨリビメ|その他のタマヨリビメと呼ばれる人物・女神|タマヨリビメ}}{{基礎情報 日本の神 | 名 = 玉依毘売 ／ 玉依姫 | 世代名 = | 先代 = | 次代 = | 神祇 = [[国津神]] | 全名 = 玉依毘売 ／ 玉依姫 | 別名 = 玉依毘売命 | 別称 = | 神階 = | 神格 = | 陵所 = | 父 = [[大綿津見神]]（綿津見大神、海童、豊玉彦） | 親 = | 配偶者 = [[鵜草葺不合命]]、[[火折尊]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 子 = [[五瀬命]]
[[稲氷命]]
[[御毛沼命]]
[[若御毛沼命]]（[[神武天皇]]）
[[武位起命]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 宮 = | 神社 = [[霧島神宮]]、[[高千穂神社]]等 | 御利益 = | 記紀 = | 関連氏族 = [[皇室]]、[[阿曇氏]] |画像=Tamyorihime shinbutsu-zue.jpg|画像説明=（『神仏図会』）}} '''タマヨリビメ'''（'''玉依毘売'''）、'''タマヨリヒメ'''（'''玉依姫'''）は、「神霊が依り憑く女性」「神と婚姻する憑依型の[[巫女]]」を意味する普通名詞、普遍的名称であり、古代の神話・伝承で神との間に子をもうけた多数の女性がそう呼ばれる{{Kotobank|1=玉依姫}}[https://kojiki.kokugakuin.ac.jp/shinmei/tamayoribime/ 玉依毘売] 神名データベース 國學院大學。本項では、[[日本神話]]に登場する[[神武天皇]]の母として知られる'''タマヨリビメ'''（'''玉依毘売'''、『[[古事記]]』）または'''タマヨリヒメ'''（'''玉依姫'''、『[[日本書紀]]』）について述べる。 == 概要 == タマヨリビメの名は、本項のタマヨリビメ以外にも、記紀神話や[[風土記]]で別存在の名として見られる。[[倉塚曄子]]によると、タマヨリビメとは「神霊が依り憑く女性」を意味し、「祭儀の際、神降臨の秘儀に立ち会う巫女が、神話的には神に感精してその子を生む母として形象化されたもの」であり、物語の中では固有名詞、特定の女神・女性の名前のように扱われているが、普通名詞、普遍的名称と考える方が正しい。 本項のタマヨリビメは、『[[古事記]]』では'''玉依毘売'''、'''玉依毘売命'''、『[[日本書紀]]』では'''玉依姫'''と表記される。海神の娘であり、天孫[[彦火火出見尊]]との間に[[彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊]]を生んだ[[トヨタマヒメ|豊玉毘売]]（トヨタマビメ）の妹で、養育した甥の彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊と結婚し若御毛沼命（[[神武天皇]]）をもうけた。 皇統が穀霊で続き、玉依毘売の御子も「五瀬命」（厳稲の命）、「稲氷命」（稲霊の命）、「御毛沼命」（御食主の命）、「若御毛沼命」（若御食主の命）であることから、本項のタマヨリビメは、特に穀霊を依り憑かせる巫女であったと考えられる{{Cite book |和書 |author=西宮一民|authorlink=西宮一民 |title=新潮日本古典集成 第27回 古事記 |date=1979-6-12 |publisher=[[新潮社]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages={{要ページ番号|date=2019年3月}}}}。 中世の社記には、[[八幡宮]]の祭神の一柱である[[比咩神]]（女神、配偶神）が、海神の娘で神武天皇の母であるタマヨリビメであると書かれており、これを論拠に比咩神を本項のタマヨリビメと比定する主張も多いが、他にも諸説あり、別のタマヨリビメだとする説もある。 == 系譜 == 『[[記紀]]』によれば、父は[[綿津見神]]で母に関する記載はないが、姉に[[豊玉毘売命]]がいる。 * 夫：'''[[彦波瀲武鸕鶿草葺不合尊]]'''（ひこなぎさたけうがやふきあわせず の みこと/-ふきあえず の みこと、『古事記』では日子波限建鵜葺草葺不合命） - 『日本書紀』 *: 火折尊の子。 ** 子：[[彦五瀬命]]（ひこいつせ の みこと、『古事記』では五瀬命） - 『日本書紀』 **: [[神武東征]]の際に賊の矢にあたって薨じた。 ** 子：[[稲飯命]]（いない の みこと、『古事記』では稲氷命） - 『日本書紀』 **: 韓地に渡ったが、神武東征の際に鋤持神となったとも。 ** 子：[[三毛入野命]]（みけいりぬ の みこと、三毛野命、『古事記』では御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』、『先代旧事本紀』 **: 神武東征の際に[[常世郷]]へ行った。 ** 子：'''[[神日本磐余彦尊]]'''（かむやまといわれびこ の みこと、『古事記』では和風諱号を神倭伊波礼毘古、名を若御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』 **: のちの'''神武天皇（初代[[天皇]]）''' === 系図 ===

* {{Bgcolor|#F2CEE0|赤背景}}は女性。
出典：{{Sfn|古代豪族系図集覧|p=7}} == 記録 == === 古事記 === 『[[古事記]]』によれば、[[豊玉毘売命]]は出産後、大きなサメの本体をあらわにしてしまったのを恥じ、子（[[鵜葺草葺不合命]]）を置いて去ったが、のちに妹の'''玉依毘売命'''を遣わして歌を献り、子を養わせた。のちに鵜葺草葺不合命は玉依毘売命をめとり、四子を生んだという。 === 日本書紀 === 『[[日本書紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫は[[火折尊]]との間の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産むために海から海辺に来たが、この時豊玉姫は妹の'''玉依姫'''を従えていた。のちに玉依姫は鸕鶿草葺不合尊（玉依姫から見れば[[甥]]にあたる）の妃となり四子を生んだという。 また、第10段の第1の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子（鸕鶿草葺不合尊）を置いて海にかえったが、その際に玉依姫を留めて鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第3の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子を置いて海に去ったが、その後、玉依姫を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第4の一書では、「一云」として、豊玉姫は出産後、子を自ら抱いて海に去ったが、のちに玉依姫に子を抱かせて陸に送り出したとする。 === 先代旧事本紀 === 『[[先代旧事本紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫命は火折尊の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産んだ後、子を置いて自ら抱いて海に去った（または'''玉依姫命'''を留めて子を養わせて去り、のちに玉依姫命に子を持たせて陸に送り出した）。のちに豊玉姫命は玉依姫命を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせた。この時、玉依姫命と火折尊との間に武位起命がうまれた。のちに玉依姫命は自らが養った鸕鶿草葺不合尊の妃となり、四子を生んだという。 == 八幡宮の比咩神 == 『[[二十一社記]]』『[[八幡宇佐宮御託宣集]]』『[[石清水八幡宮末社記]]』『[[八幡愚童訓]]』といった中世の社記には、[[八幡宮]]の祭神の一柱である[[比咩神]]（女神、配偶神）が、海神の娘で神武天皇の母であるタマヨリビメであると書かれており、これを論拠に比咩神を神武天皇の母であるタマヨリビメと比定する主張も多いが、諸説あり、[[宗像三女神]]説、[[応神天皇]]の伯母説、それらが融合した存在であるという説や、神武天皇の母であるタマヨリビメではなく同名の別神で火の神であるとする説などがある。 {{Otheruses|神武天皇の母のタマヨリビメ|その他のタマヨリビメと呼ばれる人物・女神|タマヨリビメ}}{{基礎情報 日本の神 | 名 = 玉依毘売 ／ 玉依姫 | 世代名 = | 先代 = | 次代 = | 神祇 = [[国津神]] | 全名 = 玉依毘売 ／ 玉依姫 | 別名 = 玉依毘売命 | 別称 = | 神階 = | 神格 = | 陵所 = | 父 = [[大綿津見神]]（綿津見大神、海童、豊玉彦） | 親 = | 配偶者 = [[鵜草葺不合命]]、[[火折尊]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 子 = [[五瀬命]]
[[稲氷命]]
[[御毛沼命]]
[[若御毛沼命]]（[[神武天皇]]）
[[武位起命]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 宮 = | 神社 = [[霧島神宮]]、[[高千穂神社]]等 | 御利益 = | 記紀 = | 関連氏族 = [[皇室]]、[[阿曇氏]] |画像=Tamyorihime shinbutsu-zue.jpg|画像説明=（『神仏図会』）}} '''タマヨリビメ'''（'''玉依毘売'''）、'''タマヨリヒメ'''（'''玉依姫'''）は、「神霊が依り憑く女性」「神と婚姻する憑依型の[[巫女]]」を意味する普通名詞、普遍的名称であり、古代の神話・伝承で神との間に子をもうけた多数の女性がそう呼ばれる{{Kotobank|1=玉依姫}}[https://kojiki.kokugakuin.ac.jp/shinmei/tamayoribime/ 玉依毘売] 神名データベース 國學院大學。本項では、[[日本神話]]に登場する[[神武天皇]]の母として知られる'''タマヨリビメ'''（'''玉依毘売'''、『[[古事記]]』）または'''タマヨリヒメ'''（'''玉依姫'''、『[[日本書紀]]』）について述べる。 == 概要 == タマヨリビメの名は、本項のタマヨリビメ以外にも、記紀神話や[[風土記]]で別存在の名として見られる。[[倉塚曄子]]によると、タマヨリビメとは「神霊が依り憑く女性」を意味し、「祭儀の際、神降臨の秘儀に立ち会う巫女が、神話的には神に感精してその子を生む母として形象化されたもの」であり、物語の中では固有名詞、特定の女神・女性の名前のように扱われているが、普通名詞、普遍的名称と考える方が正しい。 本項のタマヨリビメは、『[[古事記]]』では'''玉依毘売'''、'''玉依毘売命'''、『[[日本書紀]]』では'''玉依姫'''と表記される。海神の娘であり、天孫[[彦火火出見尊]]との間に[[彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊]]を生んだ[[トヨタマヒメ|豊玉毘売]]（トヨタマビメ）の妹で、養育した甥の彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊と結婚し若御毛沼命（[[神武天皇]]）をもうけた。 皇統が穀霊で続き、玉依毘売の御子も「五瀬命」（厳稲の命）、「稲氷命」（稲霊の命）、「御毛沼命」（御食主の命）、「若御毛沼命」（若御食主の命）であることから、本項のタマヨリビメは、特に穀霊を依り憑かせる巫女であったと考えられる{{Cite book |和書 |author=西宮一民|authorlink=西宮一民 |title=新潮日本古典集成 第27回 古事記 |date=1979-6-12 |publisher=[[新潮社]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages={{要ページ番号|date=2019年3月}}}}。 中世の社記には、[[八幡宮]]の祭神の一柱である[[比咩神]]（女神、配偶神）が、海神の娘で神武天皇の母であるタマヨリビメであると書かれており、これを論拠に比咩神を本項のタマヨリビメと比定する主張も多いが、他にも諸説あり、別のタマヨリビメだとする説もある。 == 系譜 == 『[[記紀]]』によれば、父は[[綿津見神]]で母に関する記載はないが、姉に[[豊玉毘売命]]がいる。 * 夫：'''[[彦波瀲武鸕鶿草葺不合尊]]'''（ひこなぎさたけうがやふきあわせず の みこと/-ふきあえず の みこと、『古事記』では日子波限建鵜葺草葺不合命） - 『日本書紀』 *: 火折尊の子。 ** 子：[[彦五瀬命]]（ひこいつせ の みこと、『古事記』では五瀬命） - 『日本書紀』 **: [[神武東征]]の際に賊の矢にあたって薨じた。 ** 子：[[稲飯命]]（いない の みこと、『古事記』では稲氷命） - 『日本書紀』 **: 韓地に渡ったが、神武東征の際に鋤持神となったとも。 ** 子：[[三毛入野命]]（みけいりぬ の みこと、三毛野命、『古事記』では御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』、『先代旧事本紀』 **: 神武東征の際に[[常世郷]]へ行った。 ** 子：'''[[神日本磐余彦尊]]'''（かむやまといわれびこ の みこと、『古事記』では和風諱号を神倭伊波礼毘古、名を若御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』 **: のちの'''神武天皇（初代[[天皇]]）''' === 系図 ===

{{Otheruses|神武天皇の母のタマヨリビメ|その他のタマヨリビメと呼ばれる人物・女神|タマヨリビメ}}{{基礎情報 日本の神 | 名 = 玉依毘売 ／ 玉依姫 | 世代名 = | 先代 = | 次代 = | 神祇 = [[国津神]] | 全名 = 玉依毘売 ／ 玉依姫 | 別名 = 玉依毘売命 | 別称 = | 神階 = | 神格 = | 陵所 = | 父 = [[大綿津見神]]（綿津見大神、海童、豊玉彦） | 親 = | 配偶者 = [[鵜草葺不合命]]、[[火折尊]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 子 = [[五瀬命]]
[[稲氷命]]
[[御毛沼命]]
[[若御毛沼命]]（[[神武天皇]]）
[[武位起命]]（『先代旧事本紀』） | 宮 = | 神社 = [[霧島神宮]]、[[高千穂神社]]等 | 御利益 = | 記紀 = | 関連氏族 = [[皇室]]、[[阿曇氏]] |画像=Tamyorihime shinbutsu-zue.jpg|画像説明=（『神仏図会』）}} '''タマヨリビメ'''（'''玉依毘売'''）、'''タマヨリヒメ'''（'''玉依姫'''）は、「神霊が依り憑く女性」「神と婚姻する憑依型の[[巫女]]」を意味する普通名詞、普遍的名称であり、古代の神話・伝承で神との間に子をもうけた多数の女性がそう呼ばれる{{Kotobank|1=玉依姫}}[https://kojiki.kokugakuin.ac.jp/shinmei/tamayoribime/ 玉依毘売] 神名データベース 國學院大學。本項では、[[日本神話]]に登場する[[神武天皇]]の母として知られる'''タマヨリビメ'''（'''玉依毘売'''、『[[古事記]]』）または'''タマヨリヒメ'''（'''玉依姫'''、『[[日本書紀]]』）について述べる。 == 概要 == タマヨリビメの名は、本項のタマヨリビメ以外にも、記紀神話や[[風土記]]で別存在の名として見られる。[[倉塚曄子]]によると、タマヨリビメとは「神霊が依り憑く女性」を意味し、「祭儀の際、神降臨の秘儀に立ち会う巫女が、神話的には神に感精してその子を生む母として形象化されたもの」であり、物語の中では固有名詞、特定の女神・女性の名前のように扱われているが、普通名詞、普遍的名称と考える方が正しい。 本項のタマヨリビメは、『[[古事記]]』では'''玉依毘売'''、'''玉依毘売命'''、『[[日本書紀]]』では'''玉依姫'''と表記される。海神の娘であり、天孫[[彦火火出見尊]]との間に[[彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊]]を生んだ[[トヨタマヒメ|豊玉毘売]]（トヨタマビメ）の妹で、養育した甥の彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊と結婚し若御毛沼命（[[神武天皇]]）をもうけた。 皇統が穀霊で続き、玉依毘売の御子も「五瀬命」（厳稲の命）、「稲氷命」（稲霊の命）、「御毛沼命」（御食主の命）、「若御毛沼命」（若御食主の命）であることから、本項のタマヨリビメは、特に穀霊を依り憑かせる巫女であったと考えられる{{Cite book |和書 |author=西宮一民|authorlink=西宮一民 |title=新潮日本古典集成 第27回 古事記 |date=1979-6-12 |publisher=[[新潮社]] |isbn=4106203278 |pages={{要ページ番号|date=2019年3月}}}}。 中世の社記には、[[八幡宮]]の祭神の一柱である[[比咩神]]（女神、配偶神）が、海神の娘で神武天皇の母であるタマヨリビメであると書かれており、これを論拠に比咩神を本項のタマヨリビメと比定する主張も多いが、他にも諸説あり、別のタマヨリビメだとする説もある。 == 系譜 == 『[[記紀]]』によれば、父は[[綿津見神]]で母に関する記載はないが、姉に[[豊玉毘売命]]がいる。 * 夫：'''[[彦波瀲武鸕鶿草葺不合尊]]'''（ひこなぎさたけうがやふきあわせず の みこと/-ふきあえず の みこと、『古事記』では日子波限建鵜葺草葺不合命） - 『日本書紀』 *: 火折尊の子。 ** 子：[[彦五瀬命]]（ひこいつせ の みこと、『古事記』では五瀬命） - 『日本書紀』 **: [[神武東征]]の際に賊の矢にあたって薨じた。 ** 子：[[稲飯命]]（いない の みこと、『古事記』では稲氷命） - 『日本書紀』 **: 韓地に渡ったが、神武東征の際に鋤持神となったとも。 ** 子：[[三毛入野命]]（みけいりぬ の みこと、三毛野命、『古事記』では御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』、『先代旧事本紀』 **: 神武東征の際に[[常世郷]]へ行った。 ** 子：'''[[神日本磐余彦尊]]'''（かむやまといわれびこ の みこと、『古事記』では和風諱号を神倭伊波礼毘古、名を若御毛沼命） - 『日本書紀』 **: のちの'''神武天皇（初代[[天皇]]）''' === 系図 ===

（神武天皇）}} {{familytree|border=0| | | | | | | | | | | | | |!| | | | | | | }} {{familytree|border=0| | | | | | | | | | | | | 001 | | | | | |001=（子孫は[[皇室]]）}} {{familytree/end}}
* {{Bgcolor|#F2CEE0|赤背景}}は女性。
出典：{{Sfn|古代豪族系図集覧|p=7}} == 記録 == === 古事記 === 『[[古事記]]』によれば、[[豊玉毘売命]]は出産後、大きなサメの本体をあらわにしてしまったのを恥じ、子（[[鵜葺草葺不合命]]）を置いて去ったが、のちに妹の'''玉依毘売命'''を遣わして歌を献り、子を養わせた。のちに鵜葺草葺不合命は玉依毘売命をめとり、四子を生んだという。 === 日本書紀 === 『[[日本書紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫は[[火折尊]]との間の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産むために海から海辺に来たが、この時豊玉姫は妹の'''玉依姫'''を従えていた。のちに玉依姫は鸕鶿草葺不合尊（玉依姫から見れば[[甥]]にあたる）の妃となり四子を生んだという。 また、第10段の第1の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子（鸕鶿草葺不合尊）を置いて海にかえったが、その際に玉依姫を留めて鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第3の一書によれば、豊玉姫は出産後、子を置いて海に去ったが、その後、玉依姫を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせたという。 また、第4の一書では、「一云」として、豊玉姫は出産後、子を自ら抱いて海に去ったが、のちに玉依姫に子を抱かせて陸に送り出したとする。 === 先代旧事本紀 === 『[[先代旧事本紀]]』によれば、豊玉姫命は火折尊の子の鸕鶿草葺不合尊を産んだ後、子を置いて自ら抱いて海に去った（または'''玉依姫命'''を留めて子を養わせて去り、のちに玉依姫命に子を持たせて陸に送り出した）。のちに豊玉姫命は玉依姫命を遣わして火折尊に歌を贈り、鸕鶿草葺不合尊を養わせた。この時、玉依姫命と火折尊との間に武位起命がうまれた。のちに玉依姫命は自らが養った鸕鶿草葺不合尊の妃となり、四子を生んだという。 == 八幡宮の比咩神 == 『[[二十一社記]]』『[[八幡宇佐宮御託宣集]]』『[[石清水八幡宮末社記]]』『[[八幡愚童訓]]』といった中世の社記には、[[八幡宮]]の祭神の一柱である[[比咩神]]（女神、配偶神）が、海神の娘で神武天皇の母であるタマヨリビメであると書かれており、これを論拠に比咩神を神武天皇の母であるタマヨリビメと比定する主張も多いが、諸説あり、[[宗像三女神]]説、[[応神天皇]]の伯母説、それらが融合した存在であるという説や、神武天皇の母であるタマヨリビメではなく同名の別神で火の神であるとする説などがある。
